# ADR-0014: Declarative image builds — build backends + the building state

> **Status:** proposed | **Date:** 2026-07-08

**References:** [ADR-0005](../adr/ADR-0005.md), [ADR-0008](../adr/ADR-0008.md), [ADR-0011](../adr/ADR-0011.md)

## Context

Four tiers of image production exist. Only CI-built and in-loop candidate builds are automated. Hand-built images (sandboxes, loop-openshell) use mutable tags and hand-plumbed digests. Version-knob choreography (VLLM_VERSION, REPO_SHA, WORLD_BASE) is synchronized by convention, not tooling.

## Decision

One BuildBackend contract with two implementations: Cluster (detached rootless-buildah Job) and GithubActions (workflow_dispatch + poll). Named builds are declared in the domain manifest as [build.<name>]. Digests are resolved by crucible itself via the registry. watch.paths defines when a build is needed. The template vocabulary is closed (no string injection). The controller blocks measurement on an explicit "building" state. crucible build <name> provides a CLI for human-invoked builds.

## Consequences

Positive: onboarding domain images becomes a manifest edit. Digests flow mechanically from the registry. Measurement rig can never run on a stale or half-built image because the controller blocks measurement on the explicit "building" state.

Negative: two build backends to maintain. The template vocabulary is deliberately closed, which limits extensibility. The "building" state adds a new controller lifecycle phase.

## Alternatives Considered

### One BuildBackend contract with Cluster and GithubActions implementations; named builds in manifest [build.<name>]; digest resolved via registry; controller blocks measurement on building state (accepted)


### Generate workflow files on the fly per domain (rejected)
